thread.title: Intraday Update: Dow Tumbles 260 Points, and It’s Not Just Stocks That Are Falling

author: Brett Arends
title: Intraday Update: Dow Tumbles 260 Points, and It’s Not Just Stocks That Are Falling
text:
By Brett Arends Updated May 1, 2018 12:52 p.m. ET I guess everyone figures iPhone X sales are just peachy.
Illustration: Getty Images Apple (AAPL) jumped another 2% Tuesday morning ahead of the Cult of Cupertino’s first-quarter earnings figures, which are due out after the market closes. The gains follow a strong rise on Monday.
Rumors have been rife in recent months that the company’s new $1,000 flagship iPhone X is selling below hopes , but apparently investors are shrugging them off.
The iPhone X has been hit by critics—CNBC’s’s Joe Scarborough compared it to the disastrous “New Coke”—for its price. Apple fanboys were notably silent when it was announced last fall. Your correspondent doesn’t understand the fuss. If people are willing to line up around the block to pay, say, $800 for an iPhone 6 Plus—that’s the 2014 launch price adjusted for inflation—why is an extra $200 such a great leap? Especially when they’re also willing to blow a small fortune on their cellular service.
There again, what your correspondent doesn't understand about iPhone Mania would fill…well, something more substantial than your iCloud memory.
Maybe the Cult is finally losing its luster?
Elsewhere, the yield on 10-year Treasury bonds jumped back up in the morning, rising a thumping 0.04 percentage point to 2.97%, as prices, which move in the opposite direction of yields, fell. The market was just starting to breathe a sigh of relief that the 3% trigger level was last week’s worry—when back it comes.
New economic data showed factory activity continued to expand last month, albeit more slowly than expected, but input costs continue to rise. Meanwhile, President Donald Trump tried to help the mood by extending the tariff exemptions for steel and aluminum for key U.S. allies and partners —including the European Union, Canada, and Mexico—for another month. The Federal Reserve has begun its latest two-day meeting on interest rates.
But investors weren’t biting. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1% in the morning, while the Nasdaq Composite , S&P 500 , and Russell 2000 were all in the red. Among the most popular stocks, Alphabet-aka-Google (GOOGL), Amazon.com (AMZN), and Tesla (TSLA) were all in positive territory, while Facebook (FB) and Netflix (NFLX) were off.
Illustration: Agence France-Presse/Getty Images The U.S. dollar could become a problem. It strengthened another 0.7%, briefly going below $1.20 to the euro. Cheap dollars are great for exporters, and expensive ones are bad. However, Trump’s new chief economic adviser, Larry Kudlow, is an Expensive, aka “King,” Dollar fan and the president’s views on the subject are, er, flexible. The DXY dollar index is up about 3% since Kudlow was picked for the job in mid-March.
Maybe this is why gold, which fell another 1%, looks becalmed. London-based dealer BullionVault, which handles $2 billion of the metal on behalf of private investors from the U.S. to Hong Kong, says customers have never been less interested . The numbers buying or selling any gold fell again last month to the lowest levels since prices bottomed out at the start of 2016.
Gold is traditionally what you buy if you think the world is going to hell in a handbasket, or you think the same about the U.S. dollar. Some might call the current lack of interest a contrarian buy signal. They might be right. As with all financial forecasts, this one has a roughly 50% chance of being proven correct.

Dow 30 : -268.85 points, or 1.1%, to 23,894.3

Midday Movers AbbVie (ABBV) is up 1.6% to $101.98 after submitting a marketing application to the to the European Medicines Agency for its plaque psoriasis treatment risankizumab. It also announced a modified Dutch auction tender offer to purchase as much as $7.5 billion of its common stock at a price between $99 and $114 a share.
Hanesbrands (HBI) is down 5.5% to $17.45 after reporting first-quarter earnings . The clothing maker earned 26 cents a share on revenue of $1.47 billion, while analysts were looking for earnings of 24 cents on revenue of $1.43 billion. However, its second-quarter guidance was light, and it reaffirmed its full-year forecast that calls for earnings between $1.72 and $1.80 a share on revenue of $6.72 billion to $6.82 billion, while analysts are modeling for earnings of $1.76 a share on revenue of $6.74 billion.
Johnson Controls (JCI) is up 3.2% to $34.96 after reporting second-quarter earnings . The industrial firm earned 53 cents a share on revenue of $7.47 billion, while analysts were looking for earnings of 52 cents on revenue of $7.43 billion. It reaffirmed full-year guidance for earnings per share of $2.75 to $2.85, compared with the $2.79 consensus estimate.
Qorvo (QRVO) is up 6.7% to $71.93 after Barclays upgraded it to Overweight.
Seagate (STX) is down 9.1% to $52.63 after reporting third-quarter earnings . The hard-drive maker earned $1.46 a share on revenue of $2.8 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of $1.33 a share on revenue of $2.75 billion, although they were dissatisfied with gross margins . — Teresa Rivas
Keeping an Eye on...Arconic Yesterday, Arconic (ARNC) tumbled 21%, making it the biggest loser in the S&P 500 . Now, I'm a big fan of big drops if the selloff seems like an overreaction—and a buying opportunity.
And of course, some analysts think Arconic's is just that. "We believe Arconic’s stock reaction 'punishment' did not fit the 'crime' of the guidance cut," writes Credit Suisse analyst Curt Woodworth, who rates the stock Outperform. "We view the new guide as conservative and see many levers to drive value, including operational recovery at EPS and a potential spin of GRP."
It was quite a punishment:
But not everyone sees a buying opportunity, if only because the drop complicates its strategic initiatives. "The strategic review is accelerating and will now be concluded in 3Q18, which we believe could lead to further portfolio adjustments," writes Morgan Stanley's Rajeev Lalwani. "While strategic value remains, the execution uncertainty leaves us comfortable at Equal-weight."
With its shares up just 0.2% at $17.85 today, it looks like the market agrees. — Ben Levisohn
